programme: BHLHE40 and BMAL2 are paralogous bHLH clock-repressor transcription factors that target each other and the core loop (PER1, PER2, CRY1, CLOCK, BMAL1, BHLHE41), i.e. they run the peripheral circadian transcription-translation feedback loop in blood cells. NFKB1 and IRF3 are the two canonical downstream effectors of pattern-recognition-receptor signalling (TLR/cGAS-STING), driving inflammatory cytokine and interferon-stimulated-gene transcription. Circadian clock repressors of the BHLHE40/BMAL family are known more broadly to gate the amplitude and timing of NF-κB- and IRF3-dependent innate-immune transcription, so together these four factors describe a clock-gated inflammatory module rather than two unrelated processes.
role_in_a: In Parkinson's disease, circadian disruption is a recognized non-motor feature, and blood BMAL2 expression is reported reduced in patients; NFKB1 carries PD risk variants and regulates microglial/neuroinflammatory signalling (e.g. CD200R1), placing NF-κB-driven inflammation and clock dysregulation as independently documented components of PD pathophysiology.
role_in_b: In stroke, BHLHE40 acts in endothelium and is protective/modulatory in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, IRF3 acts through the cGAS-STING axis to drive neuroinflammation and pyroptosis after ischemia, and NFKB1-centred inflammatory gene networks are enriched among ischemic-stroke and cardiovascular-disease genes — together describing the acute inflammatory injury phase of stroke.
shared_axis: A blood-cell circadian clock module (BHLHE40/BMAL2, which mutually repress each other and the core PER/CRY/CLOCK/BMAL1 loop) normally constrains the timing and magnitude of NF-κB- and IRF3-driven inflammatory transcription; loss of that constraint, evidenced separately as reduced BMAL2 in PD and altered BHLHE40/IRF3 activity in stroke, would produce the exaggerated NFKB1-linked inflammatory signatures documented independently in each disease.
reasoning: All four carrying factors are independently placed in at least one of the two diseases by retrieved papers (BMAL2 and NFKB1 in PD; BHLHE40, IRF3 and NFKB1 in stroke), and the module — clock repressors feeding into NF-κB/IRF3 innate-immune transcription — is nameable directly from the factors' own target sets (BHLHE40/BMAL2 targeting PER/CRY/CLOCK/BMAL1; NFKB1/IRF3 targeting canonical cytokine and ISG genes). No paper in the record states the PD-stroke connection itself, so the cross-disease link rests on the two diseases separately being known to involve this programme, which is exactly the 'supported' case.
support: PMID 21658431 shows BMAL2 is decreased in Parkinson's disease patients; PMID 41642359, PMID 38416198, PMID 39294682, PMID 40626361 place NFKB1 in Parkinson's disease (microbiota metabolite signalling, male-specific risk variants, CD200R1 regulation, pegivirus-altered brain/blood immune profiles); PMID 41372156, PMID 36881362, PMID 35352891 show BHLHE40 acting in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion and endothelial mechanosensing in stroke; PMID 42570179, PMID 42448018, PMID 41471264, PMID 41229730 show IRF3/STING signalling driving neuroinflammation and pyroptosis in cerebral ischemia; PMID 42396648, PMID 42196418, PMID 41795297 place NFKB1-centred inflammatory genes in stroke and heat-stroke brain injury models.
how_to_falsify: In matched PD and stroke blood/PBMC cohorts, measure BHLHE40 and BMAL2 rhythmic expression alongside NF-κB (NFKB1) and IRF3 target induction (e.g. IL6, CXCL8, ISG15) at multiple times of day, and separately knock down BHLHE40/BMAL2 in monocytes before TLR or cGAS-STING stimulation; if clock-gene phase does not correlate with NF-κB/IRF3 target amplitude, and knockdown does not alter the inflammatory/ISG response, the proposed clock-gated inflammatory axis is wrong.
caveats: Both diseases were profiled in blood only, so this is a peripheral-immune signature, not direct evidence of CNS mechanism, and the 27 patient-group comparisons derive from only 4 independent cohort pairs, so the recurrence counts (11-15/27 for the carrying factors) should be read with that limited cohort diversity in mind. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed STAT3, IRF1, BCL3, STAT5A and other classic NF-κB/immune factors as ordinary for blood, which is why the account rests on the more specific NFKB1/IRF3 pairing rather than a broader 'immune activation' story; the single-view exclusion list also removed ARNT and ARNT2 (hypoxia-inducible-factor partners) and BHLHE41 (a direct BHLHE40/BMAL2 target), so a hypoxia-response or three-way clock-loop story should not be added back in — those factors did not recur. SALL3's target set includes TH (tyrosine hydroxylase, dopamine synthesis) but its only retrieved paper is ambiguous population-frequency text, so it was deliberately left out of the core account rather than used to build a dopaminergic narrative.
